evidence.rationale: Recital names Pasadena Arts Foundation as "Owner" under the Prime Contract.

project.value: Colorado Boulevard Gallery Expansion, 2250 East Colorado Boulevard, Pasadena, California 91107

evidence.quote: Colorado Boulevard Gallery Expansion
evidence.rationale: Recital defines the Project as construction of the Colorado Boulevard Gallery Expansion.

evidence.quote: This Subcontract is governed by the laws of the State of California, without regard to its conflict-of-laws rules.
evidence.rationale: Paragraph 15.1 selects California law.

evidence.quote: Paragraph 5.2 fixes the time for payment and is not a condition precedent to payment. Owner's failure to pay Contractor does not relieve Contractor of its obligation to pay Subcontractor for Work properly performed.
evidence.rationale: Paragraph 5.2 ties timing to Owner payment, and Paragraph 5.3 expressly states this is not a condition precedent to payment.

evidence.quote: Contractor shall pay Subcontractor the amount Contractor approves on each application for payment within seven (7) days after Contractor receives payment from Owner covering that Work.
evidence.rationale: Paragraph 5.2 states seven days after receipt of Owner payment.

evidence.quote: The parties have agreed to this pay-when-paid timing in writing by signing this Subcontract
evidence.rationale: Paragraph 5.2 states a specific written period and an express written agreement to it.

evidence.quote: As a condition of each progress payment, Subcontractor shall deliver with its application for payment a Conditional Waiver and Release on Progress Payment covering the full amount requested.
evidence.rationale: Paragraph 7.1 requires a conditional progress waiver with each application.

evidence.quote: After Subcontractor receives each progress payment, Subcontractor shall deliver to Contractor an Unconditional Waiver and Release on Progress Payment covering the amount received.
evidence.rationale: Paragraph 7.2 requires an unconditional progress waiver after each payment.

evidence.quote: Subcontractor shall obtain and deliver to Contractor, with each application for payment, conditional statutory waivers from each of its sub-subcontractors and suppliers whose labor or materials are included in the application.
evidence.rationale: Paragraph 7.4 requires conditional and unconditional lower-tier waivers.

evidence.quote: Every waiver and release under this Article must be in the form prescribed by California Civil Code Sections 8132, 8134, 8136, and 8138, as applicable.
evidence.rationale: Paragraph 7.3 requires the California statutory forms.

evidence.quote: Contractor may set off against any amount due to Subcontractor under this Subcontract the amount of any backcharge for costs Contractor incurs because of Subcontractor's acts or omissions.
evidence.rationale: Paragraph 8.1 grants a backcharge setoff right. Under Paragraph 8.1 (page 5), it is subject to written notice and a 48-hour cure period except in an emergency.

evidence.quote: Contractor may withhold from any payment an amount sufficient to correct Work that is defective or does not conform to the Subcontract Documents.
evidence.rationale: Paragraph 8.2 permits withholding for defective Work. Paragraph 8.3 adds withholding for lower-tier claims, missing waivers and good-faith disputes.

evidence.quote: Contractor will not pay for materials or equipment stored on or off the Project site.
evidence.rationale: Paragraph 5.5 expressly excludes payment for stored materials.

anomalies.description: The retention article is intentionally omitted, so the Subcontract states no retention rate, cap, reduction trigger, release condition or release timing. Confirm whether any retention is to be withheld before configuring payments.

evidence.quote: 6.1 [Intentionally Omitted.]
evidence.rationale: The retention article is intentionally omitted, so the Subcontract states no retention rate, cap, reduction trigger, release condition or release timing. Confirm whether any retention is to be withheld before configuring payments.

anomalies.description: Flow-down clause gives Contractor the same rights Owner has toward Contractor. A retention provision in the Prime Contract could be argued to flow down despite Article 6 being omitted. The Prime Contract was not reviewed.

evidence.quote: Subcontractor assumes toward Contractor the same obligations Contractor assumes toward Owner.
evidence.rationale: Flow-down clause gives Contractor the same rights Owner has toward Contractor. A retention provision in the Prime Contract could be argued to flow down despite Article 6 being omitted. The Prime Contract was not reviewed.

anomalies.description: If Owner has not paid for reasons unrelated to Subcontractor's performance, payment is due only within an undefined 'reasonable time'. No fixed backstop deadline is stated.

evidence.quote: If Owner has not paid Contractor for reasons unrelated to Subcontractor's performance, Contractor shall pay Subcontractor within a reasonable time.
evidence.rationale: If Owner has not paid for reasons unrelated to Subcontractor's performance, payment is due only within an undefined 'reasonable time'. No fixed backstop deadline is stated.

anomalies.description: Contractor may refuse to process the next application until the prior unconditional waiver is received. This can delay subsequent progress payments.

evidence.quote: Contractor need not process that next application until the waiver is received.
evidence.rationale: Contractor may refuse to process the next application until the prior unconditional waiver is received. This can delay subsequent progress payments.

anomalies.description: Withheld amounts for defective Work are held until accepted by both Contractor and Architect. This is a discretionary release trigger.

evidence.quote: Contractor may withhold this amount until the Work is corrected and accepted by Contractor and Architect.
evidence.rationale: Withheld amounts for defective Work are held until accepted by both Contractor and Architect. This is a discretionary release trigger.

anomalies.description: Dispute withholding may reach 150% of the disputed amount.

evidence.quote: Any amount withheld in a dispute shall not exceed one hundred fifty percent (150%) of the disputed amount.
evidence.rationale: Dispute withholding may reach 150% of the disputed amount.

anomalies.description: Contractor may unilaterally reduce applications based on its own good-faith evaluation. Only written notice of the reduction is required.

evidence.quote: Contractor may adjust an application to reflect Contractor's good-faith evaluation of the Work actually completed
evidence.rationale: Contractor may unilaterally reduce applications based on its own good-faith evaluation. Only written notice of the reduction is required.
